section_summary: This section chiefly documents applications, military permits, clearances, denials, and procedural correspondence concerning foreign commercial travel to occupied Japan. It includes Commerce Department applicant lists, diplomatic submissions from Iran, South Africa, Argentina, and Britain, and individual cases involving family reunion, compassionate re-entry, emigration, and documentary waivers. Notable matters include the rejection of Joseph Wilhelm Wirtz’s return and property claim, SCAP approval for the Stejskals, and numerous trade representatives seeking access to Japanese markets.

subfiles.title: Commerce-approved applicants for travel to Japan
subfiles.from: Michael Lee, Office of International Trade
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Commerce-approved applicants for final SCAP review.
subfiles.summary: Commerce forwards a multi-city list of American and foreign applicants, their firms, nationalities, desired entry dates, and transportation plans.

subfiles.title: Application of Taghi Pour Dehnad for entry to Japan
subfiles.about: Submits an Iranian merchant’s application for a trade visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dehnad seeks October or November entry to purchase chinaware and textiles and establish Japanese business contacts.

subfiles.title: Unfavorable SCAP decision on Tong Won Ahn
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Reports that SCAP did not favor Ahn’s application to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP rejects Tong Won Ahn’s Japan application and directs notification through the Los Angeles State Department branch.

subfiles.title: Referral of Taghi Pour Dehnad’s application to the Army
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of Dehnad’s trade application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Military Permit Section to obtain a SCAP decision on Dehnad’s proposed Japanese trade visit.

subfiles.title: Renewed applications of Chandehari and Afshar
subfiles.about: Forwards renewed Iranian applications after an earlier clearance expired unused.
subfiles.summary: Chandehari and Afshar request new November or December entry dates after failing to use their prior theater clearance.

subfiles.title: Applications of Chandehari and Afshar
subfiles.about: Resubmits two Iranian merchants’ applications for trade travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The merchants describe prewar Japanese trade in textiles, rubber goods, chinaware, hardware, and asafetida and request joint travel.

subfiles.title: Clearance for Afshar and Chandehari
subfiles.about: Confirms sixty-day military clearance for both Iranian applicants.
subfiles.summary: Afshar and Chandehari may enter Japan between November 15 and December 15, 1948.

subfiles.title: Notification to Tehran of Iranian merchant clearances
subfiles.about: Authorizes notice that Afshar and Chandehari may enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is instructed to document their sixty-day clearances and requirement for two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Request for more information about Zeki Keribar
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Requests details of the goods Keribar intends to buy and sell.
subfiles.summary: Theater headquarters requires additional commercial information before considering Keribar’s application.

subfiles.title: Military permit issued to Abraham Gabbay
subfiles.about: Forwards military permit 9347 for a return journey to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Gabbay may enter Japan between September 1 and October 1, 1948.

subfiles.title: Abraham Gabbay application to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests permission to import Japanese goods, export American goods, and establish representation.
subfiles.summary: Gabbay proposes a two-month visit to Tokyo, Yokohama, and other cities to trade chinaware, toys, silk, and American products.

subfiles.title: Commerce-approved applicants, August 1948 list
subfiles.from: Michael Lee, Office of International Trade
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits another group of Commerce-approved Japan travel applicants.
subfiles.summary: The list records applicants, firms, citizenship, desired entry windows, and proposed air or sea travel from several American cities.

subfiles.title: American Nile request for a two-entry permit
subfiles.about: Requests a permit allowing David Gahtan to enter Japan twice.
subfiles.summary: American Nile seeks two entries because Gahtan plans to visit Japan before and after a Hong Kong trip.

subfiles.title: David Gahtan application to visit Japan
subfiles.from: David J. Gahtan and American Nile Corporation
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks permission for an Iraqi representative to purchase Japanese textiles.
subfiles.summary: Gahtan proposes buying grey piece goods for finishing and export to the Middle East and Africa during a three-month visit.

subfiles.title: Military permit issued to David Gahtan
subfiles.about: Forwards military permit 9348 for one return journey to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Gahtan may enter Japan between October 1 and November 1, 1948.

subfiles.title: Military permit issued to Henry Pollack
subfiles.about: Forwards military permit 9331 for one return journey to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Pollack may enter Japan between October 1 and November 1, 1948.

subfiles.title: Henry Pollack application to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State and SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests permission to establish Japanese representation for textile trading.
subfiles.summary: Pollack plans a three-week visit to Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya, Osaka, and Kobe to develop cotton-textile trade.

subfiles.title: Request to amend David Gahtan’s permit
subfiles.about: Asks State to amend Gahtan’s permit in accordance with the earlier two-entry request.
subfiles.summary: American Nile notes that permit 9348 authorizes only one return journey.

subfiles.title: Telephone note concerning Gahtan’s re-entry permit
subfiles.about: Records Gahtan’s inquiry about a missing U.S. re-entry permit.
subfiles.summary: Staff agree to contact immigration authorities despite re-entry permits normally falling outside the division’s work.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Gahtan’s requested permit amendment
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP authority and limitations on Gahtan’s military permit.
subfiles.summary: State explains that entry authority rests with SCAP, permits normally have short entry windows, and a later re-entry requires separate action.

subfiles.title: English translation of Argentine Embassy note 630
subfiles.about: Requests assistance with three Japanese emigrants’ departure for Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Argentina has granted entry permits to Seigui Hanashiro, Anden Uchima, and Tosi Hanashiro Uchima.

subfiles.title: Argentine Embassy note 630
subfiles.about: Spanish original requesting facilities for three Japanese citizens leaving for Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The note identifies the emigrants, their Argentine landing-permit numbers, and their Okinawa residence.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning Japanese emigrants to Argentina
subfiles.about: Defers action pending clarification of representation of Argentine interests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State notes that the Swedish Mission represents Argentine interests and postpones the request until a diplomatic-representation issue is resolved.

subfiles.title: Referral of Reza Kachantchi’s application
subfiles.about: Forwards an Iranian merchant’s application and sponsorship letter for Army consideration.
subfiles.summary: State requests a theater-clearance decision on Reza Kachantchi’s proposed business visit.

subfiles.title: Military Permit Branch action form for London telegram
subfiles.about: Blank action memorandum associated with a telegram to London.
subfiles.summary: No applicant, decision, or entry period is entered on the form.

subfiles.title: Pollack request for clarification of permit duration
subfiles.about: Asks whether the sixty-day stay begins on Pollack’s actual entry date.
subfiles.summary: Pollack seeks confirmation that he may enter during October and remain sixty days afterward.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Reza Kachantchi’s application
subfiles.about: Transmits an Iranian merchant’s military-permit application to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy forwards Kachantchi’s triplicate application for referral to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Reza Kachantchi military-permit application
subfiles.about: Requests a return permit for a three-month commercial visit to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Kachantchi describes Iranian nationality, recent travel, business addresses, and plans to trade textiles, ironware, chemicals, and other merchandise.

subfiles.title: Ahvaz Chamber sponsorship letter for Reza Kashani
subfiles.to: Iranian ministries and Tehran Chamber of Commerce
subfiles.about: Recommends Reza Kashani to Iranian trade representatives abroad.
subfiles.summary: The Chamber identifies him as a leading Khuzestan import-export merchant traveling on business.

subfiles.title: Clearance telegram for Reza Kachantchi
subfiles.about: Reports permission for Kachantchi to enter Japan during November.
subfiles.summary: The telegram authorizes a ninety-day stay, requires photographs, and permits a certified telegram copy as documentation.

subfiles.title: Fragment of Protective Services letter
subfiles.about: Preserves only a closing reference and Chappell’s signature block.
subfiles.summary: The substantive text and recipient are absent or illegible.

subfiles.title: Passport endorsement authorization for Herbert Warfel
subfiles.about: Authorizes endorsement of Warfel’s passport with Army clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy may record that Herbert Warfel has Department of the Army clearance.

subfiles.title: Houshang Ansary application, original despatch
subfiles.about: Submits Ansary’s application to establish a Japanese branch office.
subfiles.summary: Ansary would expedite shipments purchased by Djafar Akhavan and requests entry at the earliest possible date.

subfiles.title: Houshang Ansary application, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Duplicate annotated copy of the Ansary trade application.
subfiles.summary: The copy repeats Ansary’s proposed branch-office and shipment-expediting duties in Japan.

subfiles.title: Referral of Houshang Ansary’s application
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Ansary’s proposed commercial entry.
subfiles.summary: State summarizes Ansary’s sponsorship, planned branch office, languages, and Iranian passport.

subfiles.title: Referral of Mr. da Silva’s application
subfiles.about: Requests consideration of a British-passport holder’s commercial visit from Manila.
subfiles.summary: Da Silva proposes a thirty-to-sixty-day trip to buy metal and plumbing equipment.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting James Barnes’s application
subfiles.about: Reports an Argentine representative’s request for rapid entry to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Barnes seeks to sell Swift packing-house products in Japan.

subfiles.title: Referral of James Marsden Barnes’s application
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Barnes’s proposed sales trip.
subfiles.summary: Barnes plans a sixty-day Pan American Airways trip to sell Swift International packing-house products.

subfiles.title: South African note transmitting Pincus Vnuk’s application
subfiles.from: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Transmits a government-sponsored South African application for admission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Legation requests notice of the decision on Pincus Vnuk’s application.

subfiles.title: Pincus Vnuk business-visit application
subfiles.about: Requests a sixty-day trip to negotiate contracts and purchase goods.
subfiles.summary: Vnuk represents Linn Brothers & Lawrie in textiles and hardware and proposes air travel.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Pincus Vnuk’s military permit
subfiles.to: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: Forwards Vnuk’s Army permit and discusses delivery and exit documentation.
subfiles.summary: Permit 1108 allows entry between September 30 and October 30; State offers to arrange waiver of U.S. exit requirements.

subfiles.title: Military clearance for Pincus Vnuk
subfiles.about: Confirms Vnuk’s sixty-day clearance and revised entry window.
subfiles.summary: Vnuk is cleared to enter Japan between September 30 and October 30, 1948.

subfiles.title: Referral of Pincus Vnuk’s application to SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP review of the South African-sponsored trade application.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Vnuk’s application and asks the Army to report the decision.

subfiles.title: Conversation about Jakob Szpiro’s expired entry window
subfiles.about: Records a request to extend Szpiro’s deadline for entering Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Mellor explains that an unused permit cannot be amended and Szpiro must submit a new Commerce application.

subfiles.title: Entry-period telegram for Milos George Stejskal
subfiles.about: Specifies Stejskal’s entry dates and allows any authorized entry point.
subfiles.summary: Stejskal may enter Japan between September 15 and November 15, 1948.

subfiles.title: Compassionate re-entry approval for the Stejskals
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP approval for Milos and Olga Stejskal to re-enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The couple may use a certified telegram copy as documentation for compassionate re-entry.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum approving Stejskal re-entry
subfiles.about: Directs diplomatic notification of the Stejskals’ compassionate approval.
subfiles.summary: SCAP has approved Milos and Olga Stejskal’s return to Japan.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Stejskal entry arrangements
subfiles.about: Explains how officials established the Stejskals’ dates and optional entry point.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Mellor and Major Larson settle a sixty-day entry window and allow any authorized Japanese entry point because the underlying application is unavailable.

subfiles.title: Joseph Wilhelm Wirtz application and background report
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of a German doctor’s return to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Wirtz seeks to recover surgical equipment and resume medical practice. The airgram reviews his German, Japanese, and Chinese career, Nazi affiliation and claimed resignation, wartime flight, repatriation avoidance, and recent evacuation from Taiyuan, while recommending against admission.

subfiles.title: Denial of Joseph Wirtz’s re-entry and property claim
subfiles.about: Rejects Wirtz’s return to Japan and recovery of claimed equipment.
subfiles.summary: State declares re-entry out of the question and says releasing German-owned property would violate SCAP directives.

subfiles.title: Record of consultations on the Wirtz case
subfiles.about: Records an interoffice decision against releasing Wirtz’s claimed property.
subfiles.summary: State and Army officials agree that SCAP policy bars release of property claimed by German nationals.

subfiles.title: Additional information on Harry Julius Hurwitz
subfiles.about: Supplies the requested description of goods Hurwitz plans to purchase.
subfiles.summary: The South African Legation reports that Hurwitz intends to buy general merchandise in Japan.

subfiles.title: South African reply concerning Hurwitz’s purchases
subfiles.from: Minister of the Union of South Africa
subfiles.about: States that Hurwitz plans to purchase general merchandise in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Legation provides the information requested by State and asks for the application’s outcome.

subfiles.title: Notification of Hurwitz’s Japan clearance
subfiles.to: South African Chargé d’Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Reports Hurwitz’s approved entry period and documentation requirements.
subfiles.summary: Hurwitz may enter between September 20 and October 20 for sixty days; his passport should bear the prescribed SCAP clearance statement.

subfiles.title: Military clearance for Harry Julius Hurwitz
subfiles.about: Confirms a sixty-day clearance for Hurwitz.
subfiles.summary: Hurwitz is cleared to enter Japan between September 20 and October 20, 1948.

subfiles.title: William Hunt & Company transmittal cover
subfiles.about: Addressed company cover associated with the Enz application.
subfiles.summary: The page contains company letterhead, addressee information, and receipt markings.

subfiles.title: Application request for Mrs. Karl Enz
subfiles.about: Transmits Mrs. Enz’s application to join her husband in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mrs. Enz plans to sail from Los Angeles and arrive in Tokyo around November 13.

subfiles.title: Return of Mrs. Enz’s application
subfiles.about: Explains that Mrs. Enz should apply through Swiss authorities.
subfiles.summary: Because Switzerland maintains a Tokyo liaison mission, State returns the application and recommends contacting Swiss diplomatic offices.

subfiles.title: Commerce-approved applicants for Japan and Korea
subfiles.from: Michael Lee, Office of International Trade
subfiles.to: Herbert Corkran Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Commerce-approved applicants and redirects Victor Mattuck’s misrouted application.
subfiles.summary: The attached lists identify applicants, firms, citizenship or residence, requested dates, transportation, and whether they also sought Korean entry. Commerce notes that Victor Mattuck’s application was mistakenly sent to the Passport Division and will be forwarded to Protective Services.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum addressed cover page
subfiles.about: Addressed company cover preceding the Dennis permit request.
subfiles.summary: The page contains letterhead and the Passport Division addressee.

subfiles.title: Request for Leslie Cecil Dennis’s military permit
subfiles.about: Requests a Japan military permit for the company’s incoming chief accountant.
subfiles.summary: Dennis will support petroleum distribution in Japan and expects to travel from the West Coast in early October.

subfiles.title: Conversation about Leslie Dennis’s travel documents
subfiles.about: Records revised travel plans and arrangements for Dennis’s permits.
subfiles.summary: Dennis will fly from San Francisco on October 8; State will send his military permit and arrange an exit-permit waiver.

subfiles.title: Documentary waiver for Leslie Cecil Dennis
subfiles.about: Records waiver of Dennis’s U.S. exit-permit requirement.
subfiles.summary: The waiver covers his October 8 Pan American Airways departure from San Francisco.
